linh: Heads-up — nightly perf (ci/nightly/xlarge) shows median RSS up ~12% after deploy 8f4a2c3. A few canaries hit OOM during warmup. Anyone touched the KV cache or batching recently? cc @aj @maya

aj: saw that alert. which job id & timestamp? I can attach heap profiles from the runner.

linh: job id 2026-03-12_03:22:11, logs here: /artifacts/ci/2026-03-12/1768290011/logs.txt. There are repeated allocations in decode loop around token 120-180. Heap snapshot uploaded to /artifacts/ci/1768290011/heap.pb.gz

maya: I didn't change the kv cache logic in my last PR, but I did tweak batcher thresholds (PR #1289) — lowered max-batch-delay to reduce latency. Not sure that would increase RSS though.

devon: quick checklist: 1) is this fragmentation or a leak? 2) try tcmalloc/jemalloc stats + sampled allocs 3) try MALLOC_ARENA_MAX tweak to confirm arena fragmentation.

aj: I'm starting a live capture on the canary now. Commands I use locally for heap dumps:
```bash
# trigger gperftools heap dump (if compiled with tcmalloc)
kill -USR2 $(pidof runtime)

# gcore fallback
gdb -p $(pidof runtime) -ex 'gcore' -ex detach -ex quit

# pprof HTTP endpoint (if enabled)
curl -sS "http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap?seconds=30" > /tmp/heap.pb
```

linh: running those now on the failing instance. also enabling jemalloc stats: `MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true` and setting `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` temporarily to see effect. Will post results in ~10m.

profiling-bot: nightly-run:1768290011 detected mem-spike +12% vs baseline; created alert #ops-inc-489; attaching baseline comparison graph.

maya: another quick reproducible step: run with `--kvcache-debug=alloc-sample=1000` to get sampled allocation traces from the cache (only adds small overhead). If samples point to cache insert paths, we can narrow down to key size or value retention.

devon: if samples don't show cache, use `malloc_trim(0)` / jemalloc `arena.<n>.purge` to see RSS drop — if RSS drops it's fragmentation. If not, likely retained heap objects (leak).

linh: results: after `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2` RSS dropped ~8% but spike still ~4% above baseline. tcmalloc heapdump shows large number of small objects (~96 bytes) allocated by `kv::entry::serialize` in stack traces.

aj: that points to cache serialization path. @maya do you have any changes to key compression or serialization in your patches?

maya: I changed serialization to include a short metadata header (6 bytes) to help routing — shouldn't increase object count though. I'll grep for new allocations.

devon: for mitigation, we can: 1) revert header change in a hotfix, or 2) enable periodic compacting of cache (evict and reinsert with compact serializer). Hotfix is faster if break is confirmed.

linh: attaching sampled alloc log: /artifacts/ci/1768290011/alloc-samples.txt (shows many hits to `kv::entry::serialize` and `std::string::append`).

aj: good find. I'll open a quick PR to revert the metadata header change and run a canary build.

maya: ack — I'll stand by to roll forward if PR fixes it. Also will add a unit test to assert serialized size doesn't grow unexpectedly.

sre-bot: canary deployment scheduled for 2026-03-12T04:10:00Z (canary-1768290500). Monitoring memory, CPU, and OOMs.

linh: thanks everyone. Next steps: (1) aj runs hotfix canary (2) devon prepares jemalloc arena purge script if needed (3) maya adds test & checks serializer memory churn. I'll keep the heap dumps and sampled logs linked in the incident ticket.

aj: pinging this thread when canary is green or if OOMs recur. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident #ops-inc-489 updated: assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2.
